subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finbot.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Samira / Alex —

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Unit economics: token / inference cost is the primary blocker for wider feature rollout (esp. real-time chat flows).
- Latency spikes at peak (some 95/99p > 400ms) that hurt UX for power users.
- Ops complexity: managing multiple model variants (v1/v2) and caching misses during bursts.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Self-hosted inference on GCP (NVIDIA A100 / Triton) for prod.
- Orchestration via internal Kubernetes cluster; dev/prod model versions pinned.
- Serving pattern: dedicated pods per model; caching at app layer (inconsistent hit-rate).

Success criteria you gave (summarized):
- Reduce inference unit cost by ~30–40% (target: make new feature economics positive).
- Keep 99th-percentile latency under ~200ms for single-request flows.
- No measurable degradation in model quality (<= 2% drop on your eval set).

Openness to optimizations:
- You said you’re open to quantization (int8) experiments if we can validate accuracy.
- Comfortable with batching and caching changes if UX is preserved.

Agreed next steps:
1) We’ll send a pricing/efficiency estimate and a short PoC plan (attached: redwood-pricing-estimate-v1.pdf).
2) Technical deep-dive with Ben to walk workload characteristics and potential batching/caching approaches — Ben suggested a 45–60m session.
3) You’ll share: current infra diagram, sample inference payloads (5–10 examples), and RPS/seq-length distribution if available.

Attachments: finbot-current-infra-diagram.png (you mentioned), redwood-pricing-estimate-v1.pdf (initial estimate).

Proposed times for the deep-dive (PT): Thu 2/26 10:00–11:00 or Tue 3/3 11:00–12:00. Let me know what works and I’ll lock the invite.

Thanks — excited to help address the cost pressure here.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform for predictable LLM economics
From: Samira Khan <samira@finbot.ai>

Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Finance will want line-item unit cost and a 6–12 month run-rate scenario (esp. incremental cost if we enable real-time chat).
- We currently see typical sequence lengths around 128–256 tokens for chat, but some long-form flows spike to ~1024 tokens.
- Expected steady-state RPS for the new feature is ~25–40 QPS with peaks up to 120 QPS for short windows.

We’ve attached the infra diagram you requested (finbot-current-infra-diagram.png).

Quantization: Alex (cc’d) is comfortable running small experiments but will need a technical playbook for rollout and regression checks.

For the deep-dive, Thu 2/26 10:00 PT works best for us.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to Ben’s recommendations.

Best,
Samira
Head of Product, FinBot, Inc.
samira@finbot.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finbot.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Samira — great context. A few technical asks so our deep-dive is productive: 

1) Can you share a small sample of (anonymized) payloads (5–10) representing the spike and steady flows? Prefer JSON with input prompt + token counts.
2) Any constraints on response quality (BLEU/ROUGE/PERPLEXITY) or an evaluation set we should use for regression checks?
3) Do you currently use KV-cache across requests (session-based caching) or only intra-request caching?
4) Are you open to a hybrid approach: int8 quantization for most traffic + fp16 for high-sensitivity flows? That often gives ~2–3x cost reduction without visible quality loss.
5) Approx model sizes in prod (e.g., 7B, 13B, 70B) and whether you run ensembles.

I’ll prepare a sketch of batching and caching options (including multi-tenant batching, prefix caching, and autoscale knobs) for tomorrow’s call.

See you Thu 2/26 10:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
